items.title: Growing Canada’s Community Canopies – Urban Forestry Plans and
notes: Studies Grant Submission

L. Rogerson, Manager of Parks provided an overview of the report, indicating staff are seeking Council support to apply for the Federation of Canadian Municipalities' (FCM) Green Municipal Fund under the Growing Canada’s Community Canopies (GCCC) – Urban Forestry Plans and Studies stream. L. Rogerson noted the proposed project will include an urban forest assessment and analysis that will strengthen the Township’s tree inventory, canopy analysis, and integration of urban forestry data into GIS and natural asset management practices. The project would run from June 1, 2026, to August 30, 2027. Staff are requesting $89,160 in grant funding, and the Township will contribute $22,300 of in-kind support for staff time from the Urban Forestry operating budget, for a total project cost of $111,460.
Staff responded to questions regarding the extent of the in-kind services, the community engagement strategy, and utilization of the canopy data collected.

items.title: Water Capacity Buy-Back Program
notes: Report from I. Duncan, Water Conservation Coordinator

Ian Duncan, Water Conservation Coordinator outlined the details of the proposed Capacity Buy-Back Program, noting the program seeks to provide large water users in the Township, who have participated in the Township Water Audit Program, an incentive to implement water efficiency recommendations stemming from their Water Audit Program Report. He indicated a one-time incentive of up to fifty percent (50%) of retrofit costs to a maximum of $10,000 calculated based on a rebate of $1000 per cubic meter of water saved per average day will be offered to participating Industrial, Commercial, Institutional and Community applicants.
Staff responded to questions regarding educational opportunities and success stories.

items.title: Donation, Sponsorship and Naming Rights Policy
notes: Report from K. Bettiol, Manager of Community Development Kristen Bettiol, Manager of Community Development indicated Township staff have amended the existing Sponsorship and Naming Rights Policy to include Donations.

The amended Policy, now titled the Donation, Sponsorship and Naming Rights Policy includes the following changes: a) formally adds Donations into the same governance framework; b) creates clearer distinctions between Donations vs. Sponsorship/Naming Rights; c) introduces donation-specific requirements and controls; d) defines Restricted Donations, Confidential Donations, Significant Value thresholds, and when a Donation Agreement is required; e) strengthens transparency, fairness, and reputational safeguards across all contribution types; f) adds/clarifies privacy and MFIPPA handling of donor information; g) provides delegated authority to the CAO and Managing Director of Community Services to execute Donation Agreements, consistent with what has already been delegated for Naming Rights and Sponsorship Agreements; and h) strengthens governance of Restricted Donations.

Staff responded to questions regarding maintaining a balance between sense of place and brand our natural and green space, continuing with current practices regarding park and amenity naming, and provided clarification regarding the restricted donations.

items.title: Non-Exclusive Radio Transmitter License Agreement
notes: Report from C. Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services Dino Masiero, Manager of Water Services and Environmental Sustainability indicated The Grand 101 has requested permission to place a relay antenna on the Gartshore Water Tower, which is owned by the Township of Centre Wellington (Township). The purpose of the relay antenna is to provide wireless communications between The Grand 101's radio station at 540 Garafraxa Street in Fergus and their FM transmitter located on a Rogers Communications tower on Wellington Road 18 in Salem.

He indicated in order to allow the relay antenna in a clear and controlled way, the Township has prepared a non-exclusive radio transmitter license agreement setting out the terms and conditions under which The Grand 101 can install, operate and maintain its radio equipment on Township property.

items.title: Service Financing Commitment Agreement with Westbow Fergus GP Ltd
notes: and Salem Development Company

Report from C. Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report indicting Centre Wellington has been working with private landowners to advance the planning and servicing of the South Fergus lands to support future residential and commercial development. He noted these lands require significant upgrades and extensions to municipal infrastructure, including roads, water, wastewater, stormwater systems, and related transportation studies, before development can proceed.

D. Wilson indicated to enable this work to move forward in a coordinated and timely manner, the Township and the landowners have negotiated a Service Financing Commitment Agreement (SFCA). The agreement sets out the terms under which the Township will undertake the detailed engineering design for required external works, as well as the cost- sharing between the developer and the Township.
Staff responded to questions regarding the urbanization of Guelph Street, the timing for changes to the adjacent streets and compliance with dark sky policies.
